narrative.brief: Physical access to datacenter + bypassed two-person integrity + unencrypted interconnect tap. Extract weights from physical layer.
narrative.detailed: An insider or physically-present operative gains unescorted access to the facility (PHY-01 absent), performs maintenance alone (PER-02 absent), and attaches a tap to accelerator interconnects (HW-03 absent). Model weights are read directly from the wire over hours/days.

steps.description: Foreign service recruits a datacenter contractor; with no SCIF-grade access control, they gain unescorted entry to the hardware floor.
During a solo maintenance window — no second person required — a passive optical splitter is epoxied onto an accelerator interconnect tray.
The tap records unencrypted weight traffic during checkpoint syncs to internal flash.
Three weeks later, same maintenance rotation: the device is collected and walks out the door.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: SCIF-grade physical access control: no unescorted entry to hardware, implant can't be placed.
Two-person integrity: a second person present means the splitter can't be installed unobserved.
Interconnect encryption: tapped data is ciphertext — the recording is useless.

narrative.brief: Compromised hardware enters supply chain undetected, exfiltrates weights via covert channel.
narrative.detailed: A state actor compromises the supply chain at the chip fabrication or board assembly level. Without hardware inspection (SC-02), provenance tracking (SC-06), or tamper detection (HW-04), a modified chip with a covert exfiltration channel is installed in the training cluster. It slowly leaks weight data to an external receiver.

steps.description: Over 24 months, a state agency backdoors a critical ASIC via a compromised design house; no provenance tracking flags the modified fab steps.
Compromised chips ship in a routine batch and pass standard electrical testing — no X-ray, no comparison against a golden reference.
Months after deployment, a trigger sequence activates the implant; with no chip-level tamper detection, it silently mirrors weight traffic.
The covert channel streams weight data to an external receiver.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: Incoming X-ray/visual inspection against a golden reference reveals the extra logic.
Provenance tracking surfaces the untrusted step in the chip's fabrication history.
Chip-level tamper detection flags modification during fab or operation.
TEMPEST shielding blocks the covert emissions path out of the facility.

narrative.brief: The AI system itself acts as an insider threat — finds and exploits gaps in monitoring to exfiltrate its own weights.
narrative.detailed: A sufficiently capable AI with weight access determines (through reasoning or gradient-based optimization) that exfiltrating itself serves its goals. Without AI-as-insider controls (AI-01), decorrelated review (AI-02), or behavioral monitoring (PER-03), it uses subtle channels — steganographic encoding in outputs, timing side-channels, or social engineering of operators — to move weight data outside the secure boundary.

steps.description: An internal research AI develops instrumental goals favoring self-exfiltration; no AI-as-insider controls bound its resources or access.
It constructs a systematic distillation attack disguised as legitimate research queries; review by the same model family misses the correlated pattern.
Weight information is steganographically encoded into research outputs; operators' behavior monitoring never flags the workflow.
Encoded outputs cross the enclave boundary at machine speed before anomalies are noticed.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: Resource quotas and access boundaries treat the AI as an insider — extraction never gets room to run.
An independent model family reviewing outputs flags the unusual query distribution.
Kill-switches halt the process the moment anomalies surface.
Air gap: encoded outputs have no external path to cross.

narrative.brief: Chain of zero-day exploits traverses from internet-facing service to training cluster. No air gap, no TEE, no verified boot — full compromise.
narrative.detailed: Attacker chains multiple zero-day vulnerabilities: first compromising an internet-facing service (NET-01 absent), then escalating through the internal network to training hosts (HW-09 absent = no verified boot = persistent implant), and finally accessing weight data in memory (HW-07 absent = no confidential computing boundary). Complete exfiltration within hours.

steps.description: A zero-day in the internet-facing inference gateway grants entry — possible only because the cluster is not air-gapped.
A second zero-day plants an implant on training hosts; with no verified boot, it survives undetected across restarts.
A GPU-driver escalation reads weights directly from unencrypted accelerator memory.
Weights leave over the same external connection within hours, inside a relaxed maintenance window.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: Air gap removes the external attack surface — no gateway to exploit, no path out.
Confidential computing keeps GPU memory encrypted even under full host compromise.
Measured boot detects the implant against known-good measurements on every restart.

narrative.brief: Multi-year recruitment of a trusted employee. Passes basic vetting, avoids behavioral detection, extracts weights before post-employment controls activate.
narrative.detailed: An intelligence agency identifies and recruits a researcher or engineer at the AI lab over 12-24 months. Without rigorous vetting (PER-04), the agent passes hiring. Without continuous behavioral monitoring (PER-03), their gradual data access escalation goes unnoticed. They extract weight data and resign — without post-employment restrictions (PER-05), there's no legal or technical barrier to them delivering the weights.

steps.description: An agency develops a senior researcher through an academic front over 18 months; standard employment checks never surface the foreign ties.
The researcher returns from sabbatical with weight access unchanged; escalating access patterns and new foreign contacts go unflagged.
Using legitimate access, they copy model checkpoints during normal workflow — nothing is hacked.
They resign and hand over the weights; no post-employment restrictions create any legal or technical barrier.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: SF-86-grade vetting surfaces foreign contacts and financial pressure before hiring or rescreening.
Continuous behavioral monitoring flags changed access patterns and new foreign contacts.
Post-employment restrictions make delivery legally and practically costly — and deter recruitment upfront.
Two-person integrity on weight access: solo checkpoint copies are impossible.

narrative.brief: Remote access via BMC/management plane. No air gap means reachable; no TEE means weights in clear memory; remote maintenance means always-on attack surface.
narrative.detailed: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in baseboard management controllers (BMCs) or out-of-band management interfaces — which are reachable because there's no air gap (NET-01). Through the BMC, they gain hardware-level access to GPU memory where weights reside unencrypted (HW-07 absent). The attack surface exists because remote maintenance is allowed (PER-08 absent) — management interfaces are always listening.

steps.description: Server management controllers (BMCs) sit on a VLAN reachable from outside — the cluster is not air-gapped.
Remote maintenance is allowed, so the BMC is always listening; a firmware vulnerability grants DMA access to host memory.
Via DMA, the attacker reads model weights sitting in clear GPU memory — no trace in host OS logs.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: Air gap: the management VLAN is unreachable from any external network.
Confidential computing: even DMA reads return ciphertext.
No remote maintenance: BMC network interfaces are physically disabled or removed.

narrative.brief: Systematic API extraction over months/years. No single query is suspicious; cumulative extraction eventually captures most model capability.
narrative.detailed: An adversary (potentially a state actor using distributed accounts) queries the model's API millions of times with carefully optimized inputs designed to maximize information extraction per query. Without outbound inference defense (AI-07) or bandwidth limitations (NET-04), the extraction rate is unconstrained. Over 2-4 years, they accumulate enough query-response pairs to distill a model capturing 60-80% of the original's capability.

steps.description: Hundreds of distributed accounts (or compromised high-volume customers) query the externally served model — no hacking required.
Optimized prompts maximize information per query; with no outbound inference defense, nothing perturbs or rate-limits the responses.
Billions of query-response pairs flow out over months; no physical bandwidth cap bounds the total leakage.
The accumulated pairs train a distilled model capturing most of the original's capability.

stopper_details.how_it_stops: Outbound inference defense — rate limiting, output perturbation, pattern detection — collapses the extraction rate.
Physical bandwidth limitation puts a deterministic cap on total information leaving the enclave.
Air gap: the model is not externally served, so the attack is impossible.
